# Rome 46 BC – Institutions, law & governance

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Written, published law code** [`written_law_code`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_law_code.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The Twelve Tables (451–450 BC) are the base; law grows through statutes on bronze, the praetor's yearly edict and jurists' opinions. Caesar plans a codification; it dies with him. Local: A. Ofilius; C. Trebatius Testa; Servius Sulpicius Rufus (governing Achaea).
- **Rule of law and separation of powers** [`rule_of_law`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rule_of_law.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept low. Polybius' mixed constitution is the republic's self-image, and Cicero wrote it up in De re publica. In fact a dictator for ten years names magistrates, and armies decided it.
- **Independent judges and judicial review** [`independent_judiciary_judicial_review`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/independent_judiciary_judicial_review.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Standing jury courts and the tribune's veto exist; Caesar's law of 46 BC limits juries to senators and equites. No court can annul a law; augurs can, on ritual grounds.
- **Habeas corpus and fair trial** [`habeas_corpus_fair_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/habeas_corpus_fair_trial.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. A citizen may appeal to the people and may not be flogged or tortured. The Catilinarians were strangled untried in 63 BC. Slaves and provincials have none of it.
- **Representative government (elected assembly)** [`representative_government`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/representative_government.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept low. Assemblies elect magistrates and vote laws in person at Rome, in voting groups weighted to the rich. Italians, citizens since 89 BC, must travel there. Elected delegates are unknown here. Elsewhere: Lycian League, cities send delegates in proportion to size.
- **Selection of officials by lot (sortition)** [`sortition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sortition.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. The lot picks which unit votes first and assigns provinces and jurors; its result counts as a divine sign. Athenian office by lot is known and thought mob rule.
- **Direct democracy (citizen assembly voting on laws)** [`citizen_assembly`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/citizen_assembly.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept low. Assemblies vote yes or no on a magistrate's bill without debate; speeches happen in meetings he controls. Under Caesar they ratify what he proposes. Local: Comitium and Forum; Campus Martius, the voting enclosure (Saepta).
- **Secret ballot** [`secret_ballot`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secret_ballot.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Written ballots on small waxed tablets since 139 BC, voters filing over narrow gangways. Cicero thinks it cost the nobles their influence. The elections are now steered by Caesar.
- **Peaceful transfer of power and loyal opposition** [`peaceful_transfer_of_power`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/peaceful_transfer_of_power.md) — K3, use wrong, make hard, accept low. Annual magistrates and term rules held for centuries, then Marius, Sulla, Caesar. Leaving office can mean prosecution and exile, which is why Caesar crossed the Rubicon.
- **Written constitution** [`written_constitution`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_constitution.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. The constitution is ancestral custom plus scattered statutes. Aristotle's collected constitutions sit in Greek libraries. A single charter binding the assemblies themselves is unthought.
- **Federalism and subsidiarity** [`federalism_subsidiarity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/federalism_subsidiarity.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Italian towns run their own affairs under Roman citizenship, and Caesar's municipal law (c. 45 BC) regulates their councils. Greek federal leagues are known; Rome dismantled them.
- **Treaties, diplomacy and international law** [`international_law_sovereignty`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/international_law_sovereignty.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Fetial rites, treaties on bronze on the Capitol, inviolable envoys, client kings. Rome recognises no equal. Only Parthia, with the Euphrates as the accepted line, comes close.
- **Secure property rights and land registry** [`property_rights_land_registry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/property_rights_land_registry.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Ownership is strong in law. There is no general land register: colonies are surveyed in grids with bronze plans, the rest rests on witnesses. Civil-war confiscations make every title nervous. Elsewhere: Ptolemaic Egypt, village land surveys and registers.
- **Contracts, notaries and merchant courts** [`commercial_law_contract_enforcement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/commercial_law_contract_enforcement.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Good-faith contracts of sale, hire, partnership and mandate are enforced by the praetor; foreigners have their own praetor. An action for fraud exists since Aquilius Gallus (c. 66 BC).
- **Patent law** [`patents`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/patents.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. No reward for invention. Craft knowledge sits with slaves and freedmen whose owner or patron takes the profit. A monopoly would need Caesar's personal favour.
- **Copyright for authors** [`copyright`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copyright.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. An author gains fame and patrons, not income. Once a text leaves Atticus' copyists anyone may copy it.
- **Standard weights and measures** [`standard_weights_measures`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_weights_measures.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Roman pound, foot, modius and amphora, checked by the aediles in the markets. Provinces keep their own units.
- **Census and registration of births and deaths** [`census_vital_registration`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/census_vital_registration.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The five-yearly census of citizens and property was last completed in 70 BC. In 46 Caesar counts grain recipients street by street through landlords. Births and deaths are not registered.
- **Public accounts, audit and budget** [`public_accounts_audit`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_accounts_audit.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. Quaestors keep the treasury in the temple of Saturn, with clerks and the archive on the Capitol slope. Governors file accounts. No budget; Caesar seized the reserve in 49 BC. Local: aerarium in the temple of Saturn; Tabularium (78 BC).
- **Merit-based civil service (examinations)** [`merit_civil_service`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/merit_civil_service.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Office comes by election, birth and patronage. The paperwork is done by magistrates' own slaves and freedmen and a few salaried clerks (scribae). Elsewhere: Han China, Imperial Academy and examined candidates.
- **Universal elementary schooling** [`universal_schooling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_schooling.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. Fee-paying street schools teach letters and counting; grammar and rhetoric are for the rich, often from Greek slaves or freedmen. Caesar grants citizenship to teachers settling in Rome.
- **University (self-governing body of teachers and students)** [`university`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/university.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Young Romans finish in Athens, Rhodes or Mytilene under a chosen philosopher or rhetor; Cicero's son goes to Athens in 45 BC. A school is a master and his circle. Elsewhere: Athens; Rhodes.
- **Scientific society or academy** [`scientific_academy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_academy.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. The Museum of Alexandria is known at first hand; Sosigenes comes from that world. In Rome learning is private leisure in villas. Caesar's library plan under Varro is the opening. Elsewhere: Alexandria, Museum and library (damaged in the fire of 48 BC, extent disputed).
- **Organised industrial research laboratory** [`industrial_research_lab`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/industrial_research_lab.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low
- **Public library and museum** [`public_library_museum`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_library_museum.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept high. Rome has no public library. Caesar has charged Varro with collecting and ordering Greek and Latin libraries; nothing is built when he dies. Pollio opens the first after 39 BC. Local: Varro; Lucullus' library at Tusculum, open to scholars; temples full of Greek statues and paintings taken as booty. Elsewhere: Alexandria; Pergamon.
- **Freedom of the press** [`free_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/free_press.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. No printing and no licensing: anyone may have a pamphlet copied. The limits are defamation law, the dictator's displeasure and, from late 43 BC, the proscription lists.
- **Abolition of slavery** [`abolition_of_slavery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_slavery.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Slaves are a large part of Italy's people and nobody proposes ending slavery. Manumission is common and makes citizens. Caesar orders that a third of herdsmen be free-born men.
- **Women's legal rights and suffrage** [`women_rights_suffrage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/women_rights_suffrage.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Women free of father's and husband's power own and bequeath property, formally through a guardian; either spouse can divorce. No vote, no office. Servilia, Fulvia and Cleopatra wield power informally.
- **Perpetual endowment (waqf, foundation, trust)** [`charitable_endowment_waqf`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charitable_endowment_waqf.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Rich men give games, buildings and handouts in their lifetime and bind heirs by will. The law knows no perpetual foundation with its own legal person.
- **Craft guilds and apprenticeship** [`guilds_apprenticeship`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/guilds_apprenticeship.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. Collegia are trade cult and burial clubs and served Clodius as street gangs. Caesar has dissolved all but the ancient ones. Training means owning or hiring out skilled slaves.
- **Permanent public health authority** [`public_health_board`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_health_board.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Aediles look after streets, markets, sewers and food; four aqueducts (Appia, Anio Vetus, Marcia, Tepula) run on contracts. Against epidemics there are rites and the Sibylline books.
- **Fire brigade, civil police and building rules** [`fire_brigade_police_building_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fire_brigade_police_building_codes.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. No fire brigade and no police: three junior magistrates with a few public slaves watch at night. Tall timber-framed tenements burn and collapse; there is no height limit yet.
- **Social insurance and poor relief** [`social_insurance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_insurance.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Free monthly grain for citizens in Rome since Clodius (58 BC); Caesar has just cut the list from 320,000 to 150,000 fixed places. Otherwise a patron's handouts and burial clubs.
- **Trade unions and collective bargaining** [`trade_unions_collective_bargaining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trade_unions_collective_bargaining.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. The plebeian secessions are civic legend. Free craftsmen compete with slaves and freedmen, and associations are suspect as political gangs and newly banned.
